(p. 24)

quotes: "From the survey results, we reveal various insights for both the persuasiveness (e.g., explanations related to song popularity are more persuasive) and the value preference (e.g., a clear tendency of preferable values exists for all kinds of explanations)." (p. 2)

claim_entries.value: empirical — the explanation proposal is evaluated through an online participant study (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "To investigate the effectiveness of our proposed explanations, we conducted an online survey involving 622 participants in the domain of song recommendation." (p. 2)

claim_entries.value: survey — participants completed an online questionnaire (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "The participants answered our questionnaire through a web browser." (p. 3)

claim_entries.value: 622 — 57 of 679 responses were removed before analysis (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "Of the remaining 622 participants, 296 were male (10s: 8; 20s: 60; 30s: 82; 40s: 73; 50s: 73), and 326 were female (10s: 10; 20s: 67; 30s: 91; 40s: 82; 50s: 76)." (p. 3)

claim_entries.value: crowdworkers — a paid online research-company panel supplied the respondents (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "We recruited 679 participants for our survey via an online research company." (p. 3)

claim_entries.value: none — all participants rated explanation styles; there was no control or baseline system condition (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "The explanation styles were displayed in a random order to each participant." (p. 4)

claim_entries.value: effect_size_and_test — the paper reports Pearson correlations and significance tests (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "Figure 2: Pearson’s correlation of persuasiveness between explanation styles. All correlations are significant at p < 0.001." (p. 4)

"Because the persuasiveness of any style in the High group is statistically higher than that of any style in the Low group at p < 0.05 by Tukey’s HSD test, a clear difference in persuasiveness exists between the two groups." (p. 4)

The three social-factor styles did not differ significantly in persuasiveness (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "Regarding the social factor, all explanation styles (S-total, S-unique, and S-favorite) are in the High group, and no significant difference was observed between their persuasiveness." (p. 4)

The preference-scoped claim is supported by direct persuasiveness and value ratings, though those ratings do not establish actual repeat-listening behavior (PDF pp. 4–5).

"For each value, the participants rated their preference on a scale of 1 to 7 (1: not preferable at all; 7: very preferable)." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: music recommendation for repeat consumption (PDF p. 2).

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — explanations help a user understand why an already-consumed item is recommended now (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "Under this scenario, we aim to display an explanation of why the item is recommended for repeat consumption." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: unspecified
knowledge_or_concept_gap — the support supplies the missing rationale for why the recommender selected an item (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "To improve the persuasiveness and user satisfaction of recommender systems (RSs), it has become an essential research topic to provide explanations for recommended items so that users can understand why they are recommended [25]: this approach is called explainable recommendation (ER) [29]." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the study measures users' persuasiveness judgments during recommendation appraisal (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "For each explanation style, the participants were asked to rate its persuasiveness on a scale of 1 to 7 (1: not persuasive at all; 7: very persuasive)." (p. 4)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — the explanation space is organized into three factors and nine explicit styles (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "We then describe the three factors that we consider and nine kinds of explanations for repeat consumption recommendation." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: adaptation — personal styles derive their content from the target user's accumulated listening logs (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "The personal factor considers the interaction between a target user and a recommended song." (p. 2)
"As the user repeatedly listens to the same song, the service platform stores logs." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: non_generative_ai — the proposed explanation path uses a probabilistic-soft-logic hybrid recommender and rule-linked generation (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "HyPER [14] is a hybrid RS that uses probabilistic soft logic (PSL) [3] and develops recommendation models through a set of rules." (p. 2)
"It then generates explanations from explanation styles, each of which corresponds to a rule." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: pre_llm_ai — the scaffold's meaning is produced through probabilistic soft logic and rules rather than a language model (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "HyPER [14] is a hybrid RS that uses probabilistic soft logic (PSL) [3] and develops recommendation models through a set of rules." (p. 2)
